A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same IWR-Bench study, including readable equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to pages 1, 10 and 17.

before.justification: Table 3 reports original evaluations of 28 LVLMs on 113 tasks. Section 5.4 and Appendix C also report original human validation outcomes.

after.justification: The original model evaluations, human validation outcomes and appendix case studies remain present in v3.

M1.justification: The reconstruction inputs, browser executor, Gemini-2.5-Pro judge, scoring components and prompts remain unchanged. Appendix C supplies additional tuning detail without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 113 tasks from 100 websites, covering the same domains, visual complexities and interaction levels. The appendix test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 and Appendix B retain the same 28 evaluated models and variants. The model comparisons within Appendix F's case studies are unchanged.

E3.justification: Frame sampling, inference settings, metrics and selected weights remain unchanged. Appendix C retains 60 instances from 20 tasks, three model outputs per task and five raters; its newly specified search grid documents the existing study without establishing a revised protocol.

E4.justification: The category analyses in Appendix B, validation evidence in Section 5.4 and Appendix C, and four case studies in Appendix F are retained. No new ablation, robustness test or analytical result accompanies the grid-search clarification.

E5.justification: The human-judgment correlation reporting remains unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests, and v3 adds no seed or repetition information.

E6.justification: All numerical tables and qualitative case-study findings are unchanged. GPT-5 retains Final Score 36.35, IFS 24.39 and VFS 64.25 in Table 3; Appendix C retains correlations of 0.57 and 0.65 at the same selected weights.

T1.justification: The task formalization and metric definitions in Equations 1-3 are unchanged. The added search-grid specification is a tuning detail, with no new mathematical result, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and claims about the gap between visual replication and functional implementation. The changed resource-access statement is assessed under D1.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning interaction-logic synthesis, moderate gains from reasoning variants and case-specific failure mechanisms remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the same justification for weighting functionality more heavily; no substantive limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies a grid search over {0.1, 0.2, ..., 0.9} for both w and alpha. The abstract changes the repository from L-O-I/IWR-Bench to SIGMME/IWR-Bench and replaces the statement that code is available with a future-release statement. These are documentation and access-information changes; actual repository availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The references, Section 2 discussion and Table 2 benchmark comparison are unchanged. The positioning against static reconstruction and single-step interaction benchmarks is retained.

P1.justification: Appendix C receives a localized rewrite, and the abstract's availability statement is consolidated. Section 7 adds Yunfei Zhao and updates contact information and equal-contribution wording. The broader narrative and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: The contributor page moves equal-contribution information into a footnote and changes email formatting. The edited abstract and Appendix C undergo small local reflows. Figures 1-11 and Tables 1-6 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: Appendix C resolves a small reproducibility ambiguity by specifying the exact candidate grid used to select the scoring weights. This improves documentation while leaving the empirical evidence and conclusions unchanged. The revised repository statement does not establish improved resource access, so the supported overall gain is limited.
